content.text: No arbitration clause exists; the only forum provisions are §§ 26–27. Both sit within the accepted list.

input.quote: 26. APPLICABLE LAW. This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).
input.rationale: Governing law and venue appear in the trailing miscellaneous provisions (mislabelled under § 12 in the outline), not absent as the planner suspected. Section 26 selects California law, and Section 27 fixes exclusive venue in the state or federal courts located within San Luis Obispo County, California, with consent to jurisdiction and waiver of forum objections. There is no arbitration clause anywhere in the document, so there is no foreign-seated arbitration risk. This sits at the fallback position (California law with the corresponding California courts) rather than our preferred New York law / New York County courts, and per the playbook a clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined. We note only that the chosen California county (San Luis Obispo) is TrueLink's home county, which is a minor point short of preferred wording but well inside the accepted jurisdiction list and not walk-away territory.

mappings.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
mappings.quote: This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).

mappings.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
mappings.quote: Any and all disputes between the parties that cannot be settled by mutual agreement shall be resolved solely and exclusively in the state or federal courts located within San Luis Obispo County, California, and each party consents to the jurisdiction of such courts and irrevocably waives any objections thereto
